title: CRLR/286/2013 of Shashindra Vs State And Anr.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 286 of 2013
Shashindra. .....Revisionist
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & another. ....Respondents
Mr. Sachin Panwar, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Raman Kumar Sah, Deputy Advocate General with Mr. V.S. Pal, Assistant
Government for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent no. 1.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for respondent no. 2.
Dated: July 13, 2017
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. This criminal revision is lodged against the
judgment and order 30.09.2013 passed by the Ist
Additional Sessions Judge, Rishikesh, District
Dehradun in Criminal Appeal No. 83 of 2012 and also
against the conviction and sentence order dated
20.07.2012 passed by the Civil Judge (Junior
Division)/Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh in Criminal
Case No. 1147 of 2010 "Narendra Sahrawat Vs.
Shashindra Singh", whereby the revisionist has been
convicted and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous
imprisonment for a period of six months and has been
directed to pay a fine of ` 2,05,000/-. In default of fine,
the revisionist is directed to undergo further
imprisonment for a period of three months.
3. Facts, giving rise to the present revision, are
that the revisionist, in respect of outstanding rent of
truck, gave Cheque No. 001333 dated 10.05.2007 of
State Bank of India, amounting ` 2,00,000/- to the
respondent no. 2. The said cheque was dishonored on

2
the ground of insufficient balance. Thereafter, the
respondent no. 2 asked the revisionist to give the said
money; but, the revisionist denied the same. Hence,
the respondent no. 2 filed a compliant case against the
revisionist under Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act. The revisionist was summoned by
the learned Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Judicial
Magistrate, Rishikesh. He appeared before him. The
learned Civil Judge (Junior Division)/Judicial
Magistrate, Rishikesh, after completion of evidence,
passed the order dated 20.07.2012 and convicted the
revisionist accordingly. Against the judgment & order
dated 20.07.2012, the revisionist filed Criminal Appeal
No. 83 of 2012 before the learned Ist Additional
Sessions Judge, Rishikesh. The said criminal appeal
was dismissed by the said Court on 30.09.2013.
Hence, this Criminal Revision.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist
submitted that the revisionist has no liability to pay
and there was no legally enforceable debt or liability.
He argued that notices of demand were not served
upon the revisionist and the Court below committed
error in not considering the fact that the revisionist
tendered the amount during the pendency of the
appeal and the Appellate Court has erred in law in
ignoring the application as merely a compounding
application. He submitted that there is nothing on
record, on which basis the revisionist would be
punished and the orders impugned are illegal. He
submitted that the finding recorded by both the Courts
below are illegal, improper and against the material
evidence on record and the orders impugned are liable
to be set aside.

3
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the
respondent submitted the signature on the cheque and
the amount on cheque is admitted to the revisionist
and there is liability on his part to pay the said amount
to the respondent no. 2 and, therefore, the order
impugned needs no interference of this Court and the
revision filed by the revisionist deserves to be
dismissed.
6. I have considered the submission advanced
by the learned counsel for the parties and have
perused the papers available on record.
7. The signature on the cheque and the
amount on the cheque are admitted to the revisionist.
It is not a case that provision of Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instruments Act has not been complied
with. From the bare perusal of the record, it is evident
that the revisionist was using the truck of the
respondent for which he paid the abovementioned
cheque to the respondent. I am of the firm view that
the Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Rishikesh, District
Dehradun has exercised his jurisdiction in accordance
with law. The order passed by the Civil Judge (Junior
Division)/Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh as well as the
order passed by the Ist Additional Sessions Judge,
Rishikesh, District Dehradun are perfect orders and
need no interference of this Court.
8. The Criminal Revision stands dismissed.
